summary.text: Phil Gray, a Libertarian and repeat candidate who has appeared on Texas congressional ballots in several districts since 2016, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Texas's 26th District to Brandon Gill.

Ballotpedia lists his career experience as business owner and property manager, and his campaign materials emphasized reducing the national debt, immigration reform, drug decriminalization and healthcare price transparency.

paragraphs.text: According to Ballotpedia, Gray's career experience includes owning a business and working as a property manager, and he has been affiliated with AARP, LULAC and the Urban League.
Ballotpedia lists earlier Libertarian candidacies for Texas's 1st District in 2016, the 27th District in 2020, the 30th District in 2022 and the 26th District in 2024.
In the 2024 general election for this seat, which Brandon Gill won, Gray received 2.3% of the vote (8,773 votes).
Gray advanced from the Libertarian convention on March 21, 2026, to appear on the 2026 ballot.

His 2024 campaign website, as reproduced by Ballotpedia, stated goals of national debt reduction, immigration reform that lets undocumented immigrants voluntarily pay toward the national debt, decriminalizing drug use, and healthcare price transparency.
He received 1.3% of the vote to Brandon Gill's 54.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
